item.title: Marion A. Zioncheck — Seattle Congressman (1933–1936) Archive | He Didn't Jump
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: Investigative / whistleblower newspaper archive on Marion A. Zioncheck, U.S. Representative and Seattle congressman. Official reports said suicide at the Arctic Building on 7 August 1936. This archive re-examines that account through newspapers and five volumes.

item.title: The Case — Marion A. Zioncheck, Seattle congressman | He Didn't Jump
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: Case edition: Marion A. Zioncheck's August 7, 1936 death was reported as suicide from a fifth-floor Seattle office. This archive challenges that account and indexes 23 inquiries.

item.title: Inquiries of the Record — He Didn't Jump
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: Twenty-three inquiries of the Marion Zioncheck whistleblower / investigative archive, ordered 1–23. An Aziel Eliab Project newspaper edition.

item.title: The Narrative — Official Account — He Didn't Jump
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: The official narrative of Marion Zioncheck’s 1936 death as the contemporary public account told it — with archive clippings side by side.

item.title: Five Research Volumes — He Didn't Jump
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: Five Marion Zioncheck research volumes: primary documents, 1936 news and family battles, personal photographs, the physics case, and human and institutional evidence. Facsimile reader or original PDFs.

item.title: Volume I — Primary Documents & Forensic Analysis
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: This first book gathers the primary documents and forensic plates of the collection — clippings, photographs, and document images against which the later volumes are checked. It preserves the material examined in the investigation; it does not close the case.

item.title: Volume II — News Coverage & Family Battles
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: Contemporary newspaper columns record how the death was told to the public in 1936, and how the family later fought over the will and the estate. The plates keep those headlines and the disputes that followed.

item.title: Volume III — Personal Photographs & Research Materials
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: Personal photographs, funeral-related material, and research notes widen the record beyond the day of the death. The plates here are the private and documentary remainder of the collection.

item.title: Volume IV — The Physics Case
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: This volume tests the reported office sequence — window clearance, timing, and witness proximity — against the plates. It is the collection’s argument from space and time, not a courtroom finding.

item.title: Volume V — The Human & Institutional Evidence
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: The closing book examines witness accounts, institutional conflict, and the human evidence surrounding the death. It sets those names and proposed motives beside the earlier volumes.

item.title: This Is Not Freedom of Information — He Didn't Jump
item.dc:creator: Aziel Eliab
item.description: FOIA newspaper by Aziel Eliab: William Nadeau in the Zioncheck volumes; Aziel’s FOIA Binary Acknowledgement of 28 July 2026; a supplied, redacted FBI no-records letter; a gated, hash-chained public ledger of Zioncheck FOIA denials.

item.title: Press · Investigative Sources — He Didn't Jump

item.description: Aziel Eliab project paper: Rubye Nix Zioncheck in the car, Volume II estate clippings, and later legal actions against Nadeau as printed in Volume V. Captioned to the reader.
